headToHead.voiceVerdict: Bar, but only just, and closer than round 2. The round 2 note landed: Nav now gives instructions in the present, to whoever is in the room ('Get in.', 'Do not unbuckle.', 'I have already told your car.', 'You cannot change it while moving.'), and about 20 lines carry the address-plus-distance grammar that only a satnav would use. Cover the names and the road nouns in the top 12, though, and five of them are still the house deadpan: 'They chose the other route. People do. Then they phone me from a field.', 'Every passenger... Some of them damp.', 'They muted me on a roundabout...', 'Some places have been in the wrong place.' and 'So is a bollard' could each be Crumb or Maximilian, who also speak in short full-stop fragments with no contractions. The bigger issue is that Nav has one rhythm. 77 of 112 lines are three or more clipped sentences and only 5 are a single sentence, so you recognise Nav by the metronome, not by a move. Vera's shape varies with her mood, from 'Right. Now.' (two words) to a 30-word lecture that comes out as an order, and her status tells ('Right?', 'SUCH', the 'my career... my career on' fake-out) work at any length.
headToHead.constructionVerdict: Ours, clearly. Line for line the Nav top 12 are tighter than Vera's: a real turn in each, specific nouns (red lights, nine fifty-eight, bollard, buoyant, 'while moving', the beach Prince is dressed for), the payoff last and no padding. Vera's #45 runs past its joke, #51 is a speech, and #46, #49 and #50 are generic help-me prompts with no turn. Below the top 12 the bank still has codas after the joke ('Not even mine.', 'No overtaking.', 'Take the fastest route.', 'Keep the receipts.', 'Some bought shoes.', 'Picnic anyway.', 'You are welcome.', 'Good boy.'). Fewer than in round 2, but they still break tic 4.
headToHead.quotableVerdict: Bar, narrowly. Nav finally has lines that show a moral universe and not just a satnav pun: 'Do not ask who sat at the red ones.', 'All three, one vehicle. I will drive.' and 'I have already told your car.' each say that this voice is ruthless, calm and always in charge, which is what Vera's murder line does. There are about eight Nav lines you would clip, against Vera's four or five. But Vera's clips carry the voice-acted person: 'my career on not dating losers like you' and 'no questions asked. Right?' get repeated in fandom as her catchphrases. Nav's best clips are still admired as well-built jokes rather than repeated as a character's catchphrase. 'Some places have been in the wrong place.' is the closest Nav gets to a catchphrase, and it appears once. If in doubt, the bar wins.

templates: Fragment stack with the turn on the third full stop. 77 of 112 lines are three or more clipped sentences, and only 5 are a single sentence. Crumb's bank has the same profile (73 of 112), which is why the two still blur. This is the template under all the others.

Distance ladder, 'In N, X. In M, Y.' (6 lines): 'In six miles, dinner. In seven, my parents.', 'In two hundred feet, coffee. In three hundred feet, sorry.', 'In two hundred feet, pivot. In one hundred feet, pivot.', 'In fifty feet, lean in. In ten feet, stop leaning.', 'Eight seconds... Seven. Six.', 'Take the toll road. Take every toll road. In twelve miles...'. It is the right grammar, but a single 'In two hundred feet, a full stop.' hits harder than any ladder.

Packing-instruction closer (5): 'Pack a jumper.', 'Pack for a month.', 'Pack for rain.', 'Bring a coat.', 'Keep the receipts.' Each ends a different line with the same move: a mundane prep order that implies the trip is bad.
Ask for credit on the record (5): 'Somebody write this down.', 'I would like that noted somewhere.', 'Your route has been noted.', 'Cringe noted. Ignored.', 'Please rate your driver.'

Already in your car, the omnipresence menace (6): 'I am in your car tomorrow morning.', 'I will be the voice in {rival}'s car.', 'I have already told your car.', 'I decide where those cars go.', 'Strangers will drive there by accident.', 'Save me as Home.' These are among the best lines in the bank, but they are one idea, so an episode should draw at most two.

Casualty stated as an understatement tag (6): 'Some of them damp.', 'Some bought shoes.', 'So did the fire.', 'They are still going round.', 'Then they phone me from a field.', 'Do not ask who sat at the red ones.' The strongest family in the bank, and the one most at risk of turning into a tic.

biggestGap: Nav has one rhythm: 77 of 112 lines are three or more clipped full-stop fragments with the turn on the last one, so by the second round the audience hears the beat coming, and Crumb, written to the same cadence, blurs into Nav. In the next pass, rewrite about a third of the bank as one unbroken satnav instruction, addressed to someone and ending on the command, the way 'Sir Quill, in two hundred feet, a full stop.' works. Make that one-breath shape the default, keep fragment stacks for when Nav is cut, and delete every tag sentence that comes after the joke.

notes: Sources: refs/writing/monster-prom-lines.md was present and read in full, including the voice section; refs/writing/charm-notes.md was present and skimmed. CAST.md, personas/nav.json, types.ts, all of bank/suitors/nav.json (112 lines, counted and word-checked by script), the three star banks' Nav lines and the other suitors' lines about Nav were read. This is a real improvement on round 2. Generic share fell from 43% to 32%. The round 2 templates are mostly gone: rival deleted from the map, triple repetition and 'I am not X, I am Y' are gone, and the past-tense misrouting anecdote is down to 3 lines in logs and q-last-breakup. The round 2 rewrite note was followed: Nav now gives live orders to the room, the persona's status move ('You cannot change it while moving', 'I have already told your car') drives the top of the bank, 'Recalculating.' is now used only on cuts and cold closes as the persona requires, and the lake secret leaks obliquely on stage. Construction at the top now clearly beats Vera. The bar stays ahead on voice and quotability for two reasons. First, the sentence rhythm is uniform, the same three-beat full-stop stack that Crumb uses, so the character is recognised by tempo and vocabulary rather than by a move that would survive at any length. Second, Nav's quotes are admired as jokes rather than adopted as catchphrases. Also worth protecting: "Madam, curfew is ten. Your child will be home at nine fifty-eight. I have already told your car.", "They chose the other route. People do. Then they phone me from a field.", "Crumb is loyal and very stable. So is a bollard.", "Get in. In six miles, dinner. In seven, my parents. Do not unbuckle." and "Prince, your kingdom is not on any map. Proceed to the beach you are dressed for." Cross-cast fixes that are not Nav's file: the stars lean on 'you have arrived' (fix in the star banks), three rival jabs at Nav are 'recalculating' jokes (Dash, Tilly, Prince), and Brock's wingman ('Last mile was a lake. Marjorie swims now!') and Vex's roast ('also bought a snorkel') of Nav name water outright, which over-leaks the lake from outside Nav's bank.
